title: Solventum plans software separation to become ‘true medtech company’
excerpt: The software business needs “a different investment level” to quickly realize its potential, Solventum’s CEO said.
content_html:
This story was originally published on MedTech Dive. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily MedTech Dive newsletter.

Dive Brief:

  • Solventum said Wednesday it plans to separate its health information systems business that sells software to hospitals.

  • The business generated sales of $1.4 billion last year. Solventum executives have identified potential for the unit to move faster as a separate entity.

  • Selling or spinning off the unit will make Solventum a more focused medtech company, with its remaining businesses centered on the medsurg and dental markets.

Dive Insight:

The health information systems unit, which accounted for about 16% of Solventum's sales last year, offers software in areas such as computer-assisted physician documentation and coding automation.

On an earnings call Wednesday, Solventum CEO Bryan Hanson called autonomous coding a "revolution" inside revenue cycle management. Hanson argued that separation will better equip the unit to pursue such opportunities. 

"We're going to have to see a different investment level. We're going to have to see a different pace of innovation," Hanson said. "And we truly do believe that this asset, on its own or with a scaled player that's in the [health IT] space, will be able to get after that faster than we will."

The terms of Solventum's separation from 3M, which happened in April 2024, previously limited the company's ability to spin off units. Since the two-year anniversary of its separation from 3M, Solventum has had "additional flexibility to evaluate and pursue more significant portfolio actions," the CEO said. 

Solventum is aiming to complete the separation in 12 to 18 months. The company has been receiving expressions of interest in the software unit for a while, Hanson said. Solventum remains open to either selling or spinning off the unit. 

Whichever path Solventum chooses, Hanson expects the separation to be "about as easy as you're going to get." No separation is easy, the CEO said, but Solventum kept the software business separate from its other operations, and the unit's lack of a manufacturing footprint limits connections between the divisions. 

Solventum sold its purification and filtration business to Thermo Fisher Scientific for $4.1 billion last year. With the planned separation of health information systems, Hanson is continuing to narrow Solventum's focus on medtech markets.   

"I want to be very clear, we see this now ... as being a true medtech company. And so we feel pretty good about having both the medsurg business and the dental business," Hanson said. "But I just don't ever want to take off the table the potential for portfolio optimization in the future."

content_html_zh:
这个故事最初发表在 MedTech Dive 上。 要接收每日新闻和见解，请订阅我们免费的每日 MedTech Dive 时事通讯。

潜水简介：

  • Solventum周三表示，计划剥离向医院销售软件的健康信息系统业务。
  • 该业务去年的销售额达 14 亿美元。 Solventum 高管已经发现该部门作为一个独立实体的发展速度更快的潜力。
  • 出售或分拆该部门将使 Solventum 成为一家更加专注的医疗科技公司，其剩余业务将集中在医疗外科和牙科市场。

潜水洞察力：

健康信息系统部门去年约占 Solventum 销售额的 16%，提供计算机辅助医生文档和编码自动化等领域的软件。

在周三的财报电话会议上，Solventum 首席执行官 Bryan Hanson 称自主编码是收入周期管理中的一场“革命”。 汉森认为，分离将使该部门更好地抓住这些机会。

“我们将不得不看到不同的投资水平。 我们将不得不看到不同的创新步伐，”汉森说。 “我们确实相信，无论是这项资产本身还是与[健康 IT] 领域的规模化参与者一起，将能够比我们更快地实现这一目标。”

Solventum 于 2024 年 4 月从 3M 分拆，此前该条款限制了该公司分拆部门的能力。 这位首席执行官表示，自与 3M 分离两周年以来，Solventum 拥有“额外的灵活性来评估和采取更重要的投资组合行动”。

Solventum 的目标是在 12 至 18 个月内完成分离。 汉森说，该公司已经收到对该软件部门的兴趣表示一段时间了。 Solventum 仍对出售或分拆该部门持开放态度。

无论 Solventum 选择哪条道路，汉森都预计分离将“尽可能简单”。 这位首席执行官表示，任何分离都不容易，但 Solventum 将软件业务与其他业务分开，而且该部门缺乏制造足迹限制了部门之间的联系。

Solventum 去年以 41 亿美元的价格将其纯化和过滤业务出售给 Thermo Fisher Scientific。 随着健康信息系统的计划分离，汉森正在继续缩小 Solventum 对医疗技术市场的关注范围。

“我想说得很清楚，我们现在看到了这一点...... 作为一家真正的医疗科技公司。 因此，我们对同时拥有医疗外科业务和牙科业务感到非常满意，”汉森说。 “但我只是不想放弃未来投资组合优化的潜力。”
